messages.content: You are cross-examining other auditors. For EACH finding listed, decide whether it is a real defect in the code shown. Reply with JSON only: {"votes":[{"ref":"<auditor>:<id>","vote":"AGREE|DISAGREE","reason":"..."}],"missed":[{"severity":"...","file":"...","line":0,"issue":"...","evidence":"...","fix":"..."}]}

AUDIT QUESTION: TASK: audit batch 125 of the Protocol Pulse video pipeline (Python): ruling 158 (2) on the render's side. Only state what you can verify from the diff and the cited lines. If uncertain, say so. Do not guess.

RULING 158 (2) (orchestrator 23:12 ET Nov 23), verbatim in part: "STANDING, HARD, BOTH SIDES: ON-SCREEN ADVERTISING REFUSES A CLIP IN EVERY FORMAT: any advertiser's or sponsor's name or logo presented as an ad, a sign-up bonus, promo or referral code, 'use code', affiliate link or QR code, 'sponsored by', a paid-partner banner or panel ... The show's OWN branding, its own ticker of headlines or prices, its own lower third: still a flag in 16:9 as ruled. When the vision model cannot tell an ad from the show's own graphic, it is treated as an ad."

BACKGROUND (unchanged): visual_check.py's V1 asks two Heimdall vision models (VISION_MODELS) every CHECKLIST line about the FINAL video's contact sheet (stills every 2 s, both formats separately); verdict() passes a line only on "yes" (or "n/a" where allowed: two layout lines on 16:9); any "no", missing or malformed answer from EITHER model fails V1, a REQUIRED release row that no review drop may waive.

THE DIFF: one CHECKLIST line, "no_on_screen_advertising", phrased so that "yes" means no ad (the other lines' convention). "n/a" is not allowed for it. Tests: a "no", "n/a" or missing answer fails in both formats; the question reaches every model and either model's "no" fails the panel. LIVE (free Heimdall vision, this line): tonight's DO NOT PUBLISH video's sheets (16:9, 9:16) and two frames of its Digital Asset News clip: both models answered "no" 4 of 4, naming the Kraken "$25 SIGN UP BONUS" banner and the iTrustCapital IRA panel; control, the published 13 Nov video (CNBC's own ticker and lower thirds): both models "yes" 2 of 2.

CHECK, AND ANSWER EACH:
Q1. Does the line's wording match the ruling (every format, every clip, the listed ad kinds, the show's own graphics excluded, "cannot tell" = ad)? Name any listed kind it misses.
Q2. Can a model's answer ever make V1 pass while an ad is on a sheet (a "yes" with a reason naming an ad, an answer key spelled differently, "n/a")?
Q3. Any other defect (prompt length, the other lines' answers, the verify pack's key list).

OUTPUT: for each finding, severity (critical|high|medium|low), file:line, the concrete failure, the fix. If none, say NONE.
REMINDER: only what the diff and the cited lines show; say when uncertain.

diff --git a/pipeline/visual_check.py b/pipeline/visual_check.py
index 8fe803c6d..a07c01f3a 100644
--- a/pipeline/visual_check.py
+++ b/pipeline/visual_check.py
@@ -52,6 +52,15 @@ CHECKLIST = [
     ("watermark_present", "The channel watermark / logo is visible on the content stills before the credits."),
     ("no_next_shot_before_transition", "In the '-3f' still before every boundary nothing from the NEXT shot is "
                                        "already visible."),
+    ("no_on_screen_advertising", "RULING 158: no still, in ANY clip (not only the first), shows PAID ADVERTISING on "
+                                 "screen, however small: an advertiser's or sponsor's name or logo presented as an ad, "
+                                 "a sign-up bonus or any bonus / reward offer, a promo, referral or discount code, "
+                                 "'use code', an affiliate link, a QR code, 'sponsored by' or 'brought to you by', a "
+                                 "paid-partner banner or panel, an 'open an account / IRA' offer. Look at banners, "
+                                 "crawls, corner panels and overlays. The show's OWN branding, its own ticker of "
+                                 "headlines or prices and its own lower third are NOT advertising. Answer 'yes' only "
+                                 "if there is none; when you cannot tell an ad from the show's own graphic, answer "
+                                 "'no'. Name what you saw."),
 ]
 
 


FINDINGS TO CROSS-EXAMINE:
[
 {
  "ref": "qwen27b:F1",
  "severity": "low",
  "file": "pipeline/visual_check.py",
  "line": 55,
  "issue": "Interpretive ambiguity on the 16:9 flagging of the show's own graphics. The ruling states: 'The show's OWN branding, its own ticker of headlines or prices, its own lower third: still a flag in 16:9 as ruled.' The diff renders this as 'are NOT advertising' with no 16:9-specific flagging instruction. If 'still a flag in 16:9' means the model must answer 'no' whenever it sees the show's own ticker/lower-third in 16:9 (regardless of whether it can identify them as the show's own), the prompt would lead a model to answer 'yes' and V1 would pass. However, the LIVE control (published 13 Nov video, CNBC's own ticker and lower thirds) returned 'yes' 2 of 2 and was published, which is consistent with the diff's reading that clearly-identifiable show graphics are NOT advertising and only the 'cannot tell' clause triggers a 'no'. I cannot resolve the ruling's phrasing definitively from the text alone; the LIVE test supports the diff's interpretation.",
  "evidence": "\"The show's OWN branding, its own ticker of headlines or prices and its own lower third are NOT advertising. Answer 'yes' only if there is none; when you cannot tell an ad from the show's own graphic, answer 'no'.\"",
  "fix": "If the orchestrator confirms that 'still a flag in 16:9' means the model must answer 'no' for the show's own ticker/lower-third in 16:9 even when clearly identifiable, add a sentence such as: 'In 16:9, if you see the show's own ticker, lower third, or branding, answer \"no\" (it is still a flag in that format).' If the LIVE control confirms the current behaviour is correct, no change is needed."
 }
]
